interface.title: CYPMode: Mode-Aware CYP450 Inhibition Screening
interface.stage_of_work: hit triage and mechanism annotation of candidate compounds, with a small set of precomputed structure-based reference results
interface.what_it_is_for: Flag which candidate compounds carry a classic Type II heme-coordinating motif (imidazole, triazole, pyridine, thiazole) for CYP450 inhibition, and show, for four cryo-EM reference compounds only, precomputed Boltz-2 predictions of whether the motif nitrogen actually coordinates the heme iron. The structural check is a fixed, checked-in four-compound summary; it is not run on compounds the user screens, and none of the blinded challenge compounds have it yet.

data.note: The Motif screen was driven both by uploading prep/data/sample_compounds.txt (4 cryo-EM reference compounds + aspirin negative + 1 deliberately invalid SMILES) and by pasting SMILES copied out of the Blind Challenge tab. The upload the run exercised was a plain text file of one bare SMILES per line, with no header and no name column, and the paste box takes the same one-SMILES-per-line form. The Structural validation and CYP Blind Challenge tabs are built-in: they render from checked-in files (validation_summary.json, structure_track_test_blinded.csv) with no input.

tree.general: Decide which candidate compounds are likely to inhibit by the classic coordinating mechanism, and see how far structural evidence backs that mechanism on the few reference compounds where it exists
tree.specific: Screen SMILES for Type II heme-coordinating motifs, read the precomputed Boltz-2 iron-coordination results for four cryo-EM reference compounds, and apply the same motif screen to a blinded challenge test set whose structural validation has not been run

screens_never_reached: The populated structural-validation columns on the CYP Blind Challenge table. The tab's own text says these fill in per compound as a real Boltz-2 run via cypmode.validation.batch finishes, and that the hosted app cannot run it; the counter sits at 0 / 20, so the table only ever showed the four live motif columns (screens/003.webp, screens/022.webp).
Any 3D structure or pose viewer. The Structural validation tab reports coordination only as numbers in a table — no rendered complex is offered anywhere in the app.
not_done: The dataframe toolbar's built-in 'Download as CSV' icon (present on all three tables) produced no captured file when clicked on the Structural validation table — it appears to open a native save dialog the harness does not answer. The Motif screen and Blind Challenge tabs each have their own explicit download button, which did work, so the Structural validation table was the one view whose four-compound evidence could not be exported to a file; its values were read off the screen instead.
I did not screen a large list (hundreds of compounds) to see paging or performance behaviour; the only test file available was the 6-line sample, and the pasted runs were 2–3 compounds.
I never uploaded a multi-column or headed .csv, so I did not observe how the screen treats a typical compound table rather than a bare one-SMILES-per-line file.

The file input element could not be driven directly (the upload call reported the node is not an HTMLInputElement); the attachment had to go through the Browse control. This is a harness limitation, not an app failure, and it left no screen of its own.
